## Results

Let's jump straight to the most revealing plot showing how the linear covariance propagation fails for the RIC frame. 

![Radial/In-Track Dispersion Over 100 Orbits.](images/ric_frame_propagation_animation.gif){#fig-ric_gif width="80%" fig-align="center"}

Over the 100 orbit simulation, the initial Gaussian distribution becomes completely "bananafied", no longer taking the form of a Gaussian distribution. 
In @fig-ric_gif, the blue points represent the Monte Carlo samples, and the red ellipse represents the current $3\sigma$ ellipse produced by the linear covariance 
propagator. The error becomes noticeable by the fifth orbit and continues to grow from then on, with some samples having more than 
2.5 meters of error from their expected state. @fig-ric_time provides the full state evolution over the simulation, were the red lines represent the covariance from linear covariance propagation, the blue lines 
are the Monte Carlo samples, and the black line is the mean state propagated using the true dynamics.

![RIC Frame State Evolution.](images/ric_time_history.png){#fig-ric_time width="80%" fig-align="center"}

@fig-ric_time shows that all of the components follow a linear trend except for the Radial state, which is nonlinear. 
We will revisit why this happens but before that, let's look at how the ROE framework performs. @fig-roe_gif shows the same distribution over 100 orbits, but this 
time represented using ROEs.

![ROE Dispersion Over 100 Orbits.](images/roe_propagation_animation.gif){#fig-roe_gif width="80%" fig-align="center"}

Earlier we discussed how a Semi-Major Axis offset will result in an In-Track drift when using ROEs, this is exactly what we see 
in this figure. Over the 100 orbits, the negative correlation between Semi-Major Axis and $a_c \delta \lambda$ is seen. The linear covariance 
propagation in this framework is able to capture state evolution from the Monte Carlo, resulting in a better state estimate. 
To provide a similar view as before, @fig-roe_time shows the evolution of each component.

![ROE Frame State Evolution.](images/roe_time_history.png){#fig-roe_time width="80%" fig-align="center"}
